diagnostic_evidence.quote: are investigated, where $A$ is an invertible $M$-matrix and $b$ is a nonnegative vector.

However, for a more general case where $A$ is an invertible M-matrix, more efforts are required.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims existence and uniqueness of a nonnegative solution of $Ax-\|x\|_1x=b$ for an arbitrary invertible $M$-matrix $A$ and nonnegative $b$. What the paper establishes is Theorem thm:solution only for $A=\alpha I_n-T_n(a)$ with $T_n(a)\ge0$, $\|a\|_{\w}<1$ and $\|b\|_1<(1-\|a\|_{\w})^2$, and only for the solution inside $\|a\|_{\w}+\|x\|_1<1$; the Remarks state that the general invertible $M$-matrix case is left open and that Newton/SDA can fail there. The advertised statement is false in its own scope: for $A=[1]$, $b=[1]$ the equation $x-|x|x=1$ has no nonnegative solution, and for $A=[1]$, $b=[0.24]$ it has the two nonnegative solutions $x=0.4$ and $x=0.6$.

failure_location.quote: Existence and uniqueness of a nonnegative solution is proved.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the abstract (and the matching scope sentence of the introduction) with the hypotheses actually assumed ($A=\alpha I_n-T_n(a)$, $T_n(a)\ge0$, $\|a\|_{\w}<1$, $\|b\|_1<(1-\|a\|_{\w})^2$) and the conclusion actually proved (a unique solution with $\|a\|_{\w}+\|x\|_1<1$); the general invertible-$M$-matrix statement cannot be recovered, since it is false.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised scope of the existence/uniqueness guarantee and of the three proposed algorithms (relaxed fixed-point, Newton, SDA) is unsupported; the labelled results, all of which assume $A=\alpha I_n-T_n(a)$ with the norm bounds, are unaffected.
issues.title: Abstract claims existence and uniqueness for arbitrary invertible M-matrices
issues.why_classification: Every complete resolution must withdraw the advertised regime of arbitrary invertible $M$-matrices and change the central quantifier over $A$ from all invertible $M$-matrices to a thin Toeplitz family with small $b$; that is a major loss of advertised scope rather than a limited weakening, even though the edit itself is short and no theorem is touched.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and it is clear that  $\mu_x=\|(A-\mu_x I)^{-1}b\|_1$, that is, $\mu_x$ is a solution of equation \eqref{eq:mumu}.
If  $\mu$ is a solution of equation \eqref{eq:mumu}, then $(A-\mu I)^{-1}b$ is a solution of equation \eqref{eq:equation1}.

issues.failure_explanation: The forward implication rewrites an arbitrary solution as $x=(A-\mu_xI)^{-1}b$ with $\mu_x=\|x\|_1$, which presupposes that $A-\|x\|_1I$ is invertible; no such hypothesis is stated and none is proved, and it can fail (for $A=I$, $b=0$, $x=1$ solves $x-\|x\|_1x=0$ while $\mu_x=1$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, so $(A-\mu_xI)^{-1}$ does not exist and $\mu_x$ is not admissible in eq:mumu). Hence the asserted correspondence between solutions and fixed points is not established at the generality stated; it holds only for solutions with $A-\mu_xI$ nonsingular.

It provides no information about $M$-matrix square roots of $L$ outside that ansatz, so the claimed confirmation of uniqueness is an invalid inference, and no argument covering general $M$-matrix square roots (e.g. that such a square root must commute with $L$ and hence is spectrally forced) is supplied.

in computing the solution $x_*$ of equation  \eqref{eq:equation1} such that $\|x_*\|_1+\|M\|_{1}<1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The example sets $A=(2-\|M\|_{1})I-M$ and scales $b$ so that $\|b\|_1=(1-\|M\|_{\infty}-\sigma)^2$, whereas the standing hypothesis eq:ba that drives existence, uniqueness and the algorithms becomes $\|b\|_1<(1-\|M\|_{1})^2$ in this parametrisation (the analysis bounds $e^T(sI-M)^{-1}$ by the maximum column sum). The construction makes $\|M\|_1=1/(1+\delta)$ exactly while $\|M\|_{\infty}$ is data-dependent and generally different from $\|M\|_1$, so the hypothesis holds only if $\|M\|_{\infty}+\sigma>\|M\|_{1}$ and can fail. The claim that the tests compute the analysed solution $x_*$ with $\|x_*\|_1+\|M\|_1<1$ is therefore unsupported for the constructed data.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\|M\|_{\infty}$ by $\|M\|_{1}$ in the scaling of $b$ and in the admissible range of $\sigma$, and regenerate the test data.
issues.overall_effect: The second numerical example may fall outside the analysed regime, so the reported residuals need not demonstrate the advertised existence, uniqueness or convergence guarantees; no theorem is affected.
issues.title: Test data in Example ex2 are scaled with the wrong matrix norm
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol correction to the data construction, plus a routine rerun, restores the hypothesis and every advertised claim; no lemma, rate or guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The text concludes from the first table that Newton iteration is inferior to both SDA and the relaxed fixed-point iteration in iteration count and CPU time. The table reports 6 iterations / 0.5937 s for Newton against 6 / 0.8514 s for SDA and 45 / 1.0535 s for the relaxed fixed-point iteration, so Newton is no worse than either; the same section's discussion of the comparison figure states the opposite ordering. The comparison as written is false, and more than one correction of it is consistent with the data.
